{{Short description|On the dimension of vector space duals}}
<!-- Note: The following pages were redirects to [[Erdős–Kaplansky_theorem]] before draftification:

-->
The '''Erdős–Kaplansky theorem''' is a theorem from [[linear algebra]]. The theorem makes a fundamental statement about the [[Dimension (mathematics)|dimension]] of the [[dual space]]s of infinite-dimensional [[vector space]]s; in particular, it shows that the [[Dual space#Algebraic dual space|algebraic dual space]] is not [[isomorphism|isomorphic]] to the vector space itself. A more general formulation allows to compute the exact dimension of any [[Vector space#Function space|function space]].
 
The theorem is named after [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Irving Kaplansky]].

== Statement ==
Let <math>E</math> be an infinite-dimensional vector space over a [[Field (algebra)|field]] <math>\mathbb{K}</math> and let <math>I</math> be some basis of it. Then for the dual space <math>E^*</math>,<ref>{{cite book|first1=Gottfried|last1=Köthe|title=Topological Vector Spaces I.|place=Germany|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|date=1983|page=75}}</ref>
:<math>\operatorname{dim}(E^*)=\operatorname{card}(\mathbb{K}^I).</math>
By [[Cantor's theorem]], this [[Cardinal number|cardinal]] is strictly larger than the dimension <math>\operatorname{card}(I)</math> of <math>E</math>. More generally, if <math>I</math> is an arbitrary infinite set, the dimension of the space of all functions <math>\mathbb{K}^I</math> is given by:<ref>{{cite book|title=Elements of mathematics: Algebra I, Chapters 1 - 3|author=[[Nicolas Bourbaki]]|page=400|editor=Hermann|isbn=0201006391|year=1974|language=en}}</ref>
:<math>\operatorname{dim}(\mathbb{K}^I)=\operatorname{card}(\mathbb{K}^I).</math>
When <math>I</math> is finite, it's a standard result that <math>\dim(\mathbb{K}^I) = \operatorname{card}(I)</math>. This gives us a full characterization of the dimension of this space.
